subject: Earth from Moon
title: What If You Saw Earth From the Moon?

scenes.text: What if you stood on the Moon and looked up at Earth? It would never move.
First, the size. Earth looks about four times wider than a full Moon does from here.
At its fullest, Earth shines roughly fifteen times brighter than our full Moon, and you'd watch it spin every day.
But it never rises or sets. The Moon keeps one face toward us, so Earth hangs in one spot.
Over each month it runs through phases, backwards. When we see a new Moon, you'd see a full Earth.
And on the Moon's far side? You could live your whole life there and never see Earth once.

description:
What if you saw Earth from the Moon? Earth would look about 3.7 times wider than the full Moon looks to us and up to about 15 times brighter.
Because the Moon is tidally locked, Earth stays nearly fixed in the sky over most of the near side, its phases run opposite to the Moon's, and it is never visible from the far side.
